name: Financier
origin: A small rectangular French cake named for its resemblance to a gold bar, popular with bankers near the Paris stock exchange in the late 19th century; browned butter (beurre noisette) and ground almond, not wheat gluten, give it its structure.

ingredients.note: ground almond, not wheat flour, is financier's real structural base; modelled with almond-kernel's own composition (packages/data/substances/almond-kernel.json) ground into flour form
egg white only, no yolk — financier is one of the classic 'white batter' French petits fours
browned (beurre noisette) before folding in, for its characteristic nutty flavour; the browning is a flavour change, not a mass change

process.name: brown the butter
process.description: cook butter until the milk solids brown and it smells nutty, then cool slightly

process.name: whisk dry and egg white
process.description: whisk ground almond, flour and sugar with egg whites to a smooth batter

notes: A representative financier proportion (Larousse Gastronomique's petit-four formulas): roughly equal parts ground almond and wheat flour for the flour baseline, egg white rather than whole egg, and a substantial browned-butter dose.
